notes: 2605.14211 ASH (scope conflict): IN SCOPE, sol. A3 bullet 2 and the run's RMM (r02b) / PsychAgent (r13b) precedent: the key-moment memory is a non-weight object (HDBSCAN classifier K, re-fitted at every stuck-triggered bootstrap, plus a per-agent bank appended during play). The deployed policy reads it at every step (opus:O07), and two controls evaluate it: memory-off (−2.5 milestones) and random-frame content (6.00 vs 7.75). This differs from SEAgent (r05b), DreamGym (r07b) and EvoEnv (this batch), where the non-weight asset is only training data. Weight-side gains from bootstrapping are not credited as harness evidence. Final 61.25, below sol's 65.0. E.causality is revised 3 → 2 for two reasons. First, the random-frame control is stated only for inference (opus:O01), so a train/inference mismatch can explain the drop. Second, no frozen-K arm separates the feedback-driven update of the memory from weight retraining (opus:O06). son55's finding is confirmed: the paper gives three different 'strongest baseline' values (intro 6.5/6.0 = the BC row; Appendix C '9'; Table 6 Voyager 9.25/7.83), and §4.1 says 'no baseline exceeds milestone 8', which contradicts the 9.25 mean. RS → son55 C08 (IDM inverse mapping over naturally occurring video, failure-targeted retrieval, cluster gate, iterate). Domain → sol H04 + H28.

2605.14392 EvoEnv: OUT OF SCOPE. This is a shared-error correction: both seats wrote 'reviewed'. Under A3 bullet 1 the improver's update object and product are both weights. One shared policy is GRPO-trained in both roles (opus:O01, opus:O05). Every reported number is a trained checkpoint (opus:O03), and the ablations change the generator reward used for policy training (opus:O04). The environment pool is RL training data: it is retired after a fixed number of solver epochs (opus:O02), it is never read by an evaluated agent at test time, and it is never transferred to a fresh solver. A3 explicitly covers this case ('even if code is generated and reused in the process'). Precedents: CoEvolve r17a, DreamGym r07b (Opus overturned both seats), Agent-World r16b, R-Zero/SPELL. Not scored (seats 61.25 / 63.75). Informational C08 + H22.

2605.15461 DrugSAGE (seat Δ5): final 61.25. X → son55 2. The cross-task memory is append-all (every executed candidate is written back), with no admission gate, versioning, expiry or rollback. The search and transfer hyperparameters (α, β, λ, γ, δ) and the order in which the 16 source tasks fill the memory are not stated. Shared correction: E.measurement 3 → 2. The analog-task ablation reports 'TDC leaderboard best' values of 0.820/0.898/0.728 (opus:O01), but Table 2 and Table 6 give 0.859/0.916/0.790 for the same targets (opus:O02, opus:O04). On CYP2D6, the 0.733 'remains competitive' claim is therefore 0.057 below the paper's own leaderboard value. The abstract's '33 tasks, single-task, nine agents' also conflicts with the body (22 TDC tasks, eight baselines; son55's finding). Run convention: text–table contradictions cap E.measurement at 2. RS → adapt_via_conditioning, sub null (r17b convention). heterogeneous_decomposition is not kept. Domain → H03 + H15. H02 is not kept: the skills come from literature, not from the agent's own outcomes.

2605.15611 TopoEvo (Δ1.25): final 28.75, below both seats (33.75 / 35.0); each item was decided separately. X → son55 1: the memory's read interface is never described. The write gate ('solved incidents'), the refresh rates, τ/γ of Eq. 19, the TTA confidence thresholds and top-K/H are all unspecified, and there is no versioning or rollback. E.measurement → sol 1. Text and tables disagree repeatedly. Text says TAMO is stronger on B Acc@1, but the table has 75.66 vs 72.22. The prose gives ablation values 56.10/74.10/61.10/58.10 and a 'full 71.90' on B that appear nowhere in Table II. '15–16 points on all subsets' does not hold for B (19.8), and '≥8 points' fails on A_s (7.68) and A_n (7.29). MRR, latency and faithfulness are defined but never reported, and no denominators are given. E.causality → sol 1: the only retention-relevant ablation (w/o SEM) removes the memory and the weight-side TTA together, and both may run on the evaluated incidents (opus:O05). The MOMA/VQ/HET ablations keep it above 0. RS → sol C13 primary + son55 C25 supporting (C08 not kept).

2605.15701 H-Mem (Δ12.5): final 57.5. G → son55 2: the gap is a combination gap defined by the paper's own taxonomy. The table narrows 'evolution' so that EverMemOS/Zep look incomplete, and there is no failure analysis. M → sol 3: son55's main reason was that there is no execution-feedback loop, which judges a B-class component as if it were A-class (SCORE_SPEC: A/B is an inclusion type, not a quality grade). The tree/graph operations map onto both stated gap halves, and the ablations test both. X → sol 3: the static build/retrieve flow is reconstructable down to the hyperparameters (windows; thresholds 0.8/0.7/0.6; weights 0.70/0.15/0.15; τ = 365 d; η = 0.5; entity-resolution rules; prompts). It has no admission gate, deletion or versioning. E.cost → sol 2: five cost dimensions are measured, but the text gives only ordinal positions (values are in the Figure 2 image, not read), there is no budget-matched comparison, and H-Mem uses more indexing/retrieval tokens than most baselines. Paper facts recorded: fixed-Mixed retrieval matches accuracy (92.21 vs 92.01) at 1.8× tokens; top-k is chosen on LoCoMo test; 'largest gains on temporal' is contradicted by the Accuracy cells.
